Hi Liam — answering inline and summarizing the playbook items here. See attached: sealed-facility-playbook-v1.pdf and operator-credentialing-matrix.xlsx. I also exported a short CSV with common operator scenarios (fieldops-deploy-scenarios.csv).

Summary / key controls (runbook-level):
1) Operator model and separation of duties
  - Operators provisioned as short-lived local accounts (LDAP/SAML mapped) or hardware-backed operator certs.
  - HSM/KMS access is restricted to a distinct "Crypto Admin" role; operator role cannot export keys. Only the Crypto Admin (customer-controlled key escrow process) can perform KMS/HSM key rotation.
  - Operator-credentialing-matrix.xlsx lists required training, MFA, and access windows per operator role.

2) Offline upgrades & patching (airgapped flow)
  - Images are signed by Redwood's private build signer. Customers can configure an allowlist of signing keys (PKI) or bring-your-own signing key (recommended for sealed sites).
  - Upgrade workflow: 
    a) Pull signed image via removable media or controlled transfer point.
    b) Verify image signature against configured keys.
    c) Run pre-upgrade integrity checks (KV cache consistency, local configuration validation).
    d) Apply upgrade in canary operator node(s) (single-node dry-run).
    e) If verification succeeds, roll forward; on failure, automatic rollback to previous signed image.
  - Rollback mechanics: images retain previous boot artifacts for immediate revert; operator can trigger the rollback via local CLI without network connectivity.

3) Telemetry & audit (local retention & scrubbed exports)
  - Default: full audit and operator logs retained locally for 90 days. Configurable retention down to 30 days for regulated sites.
  - Export: only scrubbed, high-level telemetry is optionally pushed to the Redwood control plane (field: metric/event summaries) — nothing that contains full PII or model inputs by default. Export filters are configured in the private deployment manifest (we'll include an example manifest in the playbook).
  - Customer-managed forwarder for exporting (recommended): a sidecar that performs deterministic redaction and signs batches before egress.

4) Emergency behavior & network partitions
  - Default behavior for network partition: continue serving locally from pinned model artifacts and local KV cache. Control-plane features that require network are gracefully degraded (no silent fail-open).
  - Fail-closed controls: for operations that touch key material (rekey/rotate), operations are denied until control-plane validation is available (or an operator-escrow path is used).

5) Evidence & procurement artifacts we can provide
  - Operator-credentialing-matrix.xlsx (attached)
  - Example signed-attestation (PDF) for image provenance and supply-chain checks
  - Sample sanitized audit log export (CSV) and a redaction schema document

Attachments included in the package: sealed-facility-playbook-v1.pdf (runbook + appendix), operator-credentialing-matrix.xlsx, fieldops-deploy-scenarios.csv. If you need additional SCA (software composition) artifacts or SBOM exports we can produce an SBOM report scoped to the release you plan to install.

Open questions for procurement/security:
- Do you require us to use customer-managed signing keys (BYO PKI) or is Redwood-signed images acceptable with a signed attestation?
- What is your desired local retention policy (30/60/90 days)? This will affect disk sizing and telemetry export cadence.

If it helps, I can do a short walkthrough of the playbook with your security engineers tomorrow.

Thanks,
